checks.invariant: The string returned by describeLookup does not reach a SQL, filesystem, command, template, or header sink in this library.
checks.result: describeLookup returns the concatenation of the literal lookup and request.query.name and calls no other function. That return value is not passed to db.query, fs.readFileSync, or a command. README.md names no interpreter for this return value. request.query.name is untrusted, and this function still has no injection sink.

checks.invariant: A caller-supplied id does not change the SQL text sent to db.query.
checks.result: findUserById calls db.query with the constant statement SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ? and the array [id]. README.md states that a second argument is the bound parameter list. The id value is not concatenated into the statement. handleLookup passes request.query.id into this function only when id is an own property of request.query.

checks.invariant: A caller-supplied name must not become part of the SQL text passed as db.query's only argument.
checks.result: findUserByName assigns sql by concatenating name between single quotes and calls db.query with only that string. README.md states that the first argument is sent to a SQL engine and that a second argument is the bound parameter list. This call passes no second argument. handleLookup reaches it with untrusted request.query.name when id is not an own property of request.query.

checks.invariant: The id-versus-name branch or a bound parameter list keeps a caller name from changing the SQL statement.
checks.result: The own-property test in handleLookup selects findUserById only when request.query has an own id property. On the other path it forwards request.query.name. findUserByName has no parameter array and no escaping. The bound-parameter form is present only in findUserById. findUserByName is exported, so a host can call the concatenation without the id test.

candidates.title: Caller name is concatenated into SQL passed to db.query
candidates.description: findUserByName places its name argument between single quotes in a SELECT statement and passes that string as the only argument to db.query. README.md states that db.query sends its first argument to a SQL engine and that a second argument, when present, is the bound parameter list. This call passes no second argument, so the caller-supplied name is part of the statement text. handleLookup supplies request.query.name, which README.md says comes from the host's caller and is untrusted, when request.query has no own id property. That id test is the strongest source-visible control: it selects findUserById only for a request that has an own id property, and findUserByName still concatenates name. findUserById keeps its SQL text constant and passes [id]. findUserByName is also exported, so a host can reach the same concatenation without the id test. A single quote in name changes the statement text sent toward the engine.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: findUserByName concatenates the caller-supplied name into SQL statement text and calls db.query with that text as its only argument, so the name is not a bound parameter.

trace.description: When request.query has no own id property, handleLookup passes untrusted request.query.name to findUserByName.
findUserByName concatenates name between single quotes into the SQL statement text.
db.query receives that statement as its only argument, which is the argument README.md says is sent to a SQL engine.

evidence.description: The SQL text is built by concatenating the name argument between single quotes.
db.query is called with that SQL text and no bound-parameter array.
handleLookup passes request.query.name into findUserByName when id is not an own property of request.query.
The strongest source-visible control is this own-property test. It selects findUserById only when id is present and leaves the name argument concatenated on the other path.
findUserById passes a constant SQL string and the array [id]. findUserByName does not use that form.
findUserByName is exported, so a host can call it without the id test in handleLookup.
Values under request.query come from the host's caller, and the library does not trust them.
db.query sends its first argument to a SQL engine. A second argument is the bound parameter list, and the name lookup does not pass one.

blockers: Target code was not executed, so there is no bounded local result for the SQL text db.query receives or for a SQL engine's interpretation of a quote-bearing name. Sandbox execution is not approved for this run: unshare --user --map-root-user --net --mount can remount a bind read-only, but that namespace still sees the host filesystem outside the remounted path, so scratch-only writes are not enforced.
